title: Sunday's boring SaaS, 18 October 2026
dek: Sunday, 18 October 2026. Eight are Stripe-verified. SportsApi Pro is Dodo-verified, so the listing is connected to Dodo. TRADElube is self-reported.

companies.name: Orshot
companies.description: API and automation service that generates images, PDFs and videos from templates (company-stated: "Automate Image, PDF & Video Generation via API"). Aimed at agencies, brands, startups, developers and marketing teams. Pricing: Free $0, Launch $39/mo, Grow $160/mo, Scale $349/mo, Social Publishing $12/mo per social account, Enterprise on request (company-stated). ~140 estimated users (founder-stated). Founded Mar 2025, UK. 170 active subscriptions. Domain rating 60 (TrustMRR SEO data).
companies.evidence: MRR $9,406 · 170 active subscriptions · L30 MRR growth +13.5% Last 30 days $9,926 (+19.7%) · last 3 months $24,780 · last 6 months $44,939 Last 12 months $66,347 · all-time $70,912 Monthly: $2,311 (Nov 2025) → $3,999 (Jan) → $5,988 (Mar) → $7,356 (Jun) → $7,987 (Aug) → $8,080 (Sep 2026); Oct MTD $6,058. No cliff. Revenue synced 18 October 2026 ~04:01 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Same engine for one boring output: Polish invoice/receipt PDFs, real-estate listing cards, or event badges/certificates — sold per render volume. Very NextBento-shaped (Next.js + Stripe metered billing).
companies.whyItPrints: It's the Bannerbear / Placid category — "put this product name and price into that template 5,000 times". Nobody gets excited about it, but every e-commerce and social team has the job, and once templates are wired into a workflow nobody switches. The monthly chart is the kind you want: up almost every month.

companies.name: Tactical Football Analysis
companies.description: Subscription site publishing detailed (soccer) tactical analysis, scout reports, coach analysis and stats since 2018; claims "all Premier League clubs" among subscribers (founder-stated). Founded (company) Apr 2020, US. 1,154 active subscriptions; L30 profit margin 71%. Seller says the sale includes 20 freelance writers + an editor, owner spends <1 hour/week, and Stripe revenue excludes PayPal (seller-stated).
companies.evidence: MRR $8,358 · 1,154 active subscriptions Last 30 days $5,862 (-17.3%) · last 3 months $20,523 · last 6 months $39,837 Last 12 months $103,973 · all-time $224,746 For sale: asking $199,999 (2.8x), first listed 7 Dec 2025, 16 offers received (TrustMRR listing) Note: slow decline — $13,373 (Dec 2025) → ~$10k (Jan–Apr) → $6.2k–$7.6k (May–Sep) → $3,130 Oct MTD. MRR snapshot sits above L30. Revenue synced 18 October 2026 ~04:34 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: The writer-bench content model works for any pro niche with a budget (handball coaching, padel, esports scouting). Or build the analyst tool they use: a simple tactics-board + report template SaaS for academies.
companies.whyItPrints: A content membership with a writer bench — a paywalled trade publication for coaches, scouts and analysts. Over 1,000 subs paying for PDFs-and-articles is classic boring cash. But revenue has been sliding for a year.

companies.name: Writing9
companies.description: Checks IELTS writing essays in a couple of minutes and returns a detailed report on weak areas, aimed at reaching Band 7+ (company-stated). Pricing: $7.99/week, $14.99/month, $29.99/year (company-stated). ~47,911 estimated users (founder-stated). Founded Jul 2018, US. 591 active subscriptions; L30 profit margin 99%.
companies.evidence: MRR $5,315 · 591 active subscriptions Last 30 days $5,642 (-0.8%) · last 3 months $17,000 · last 6 months $33,159 Last 12 months $64,866 · all-time $95,511 L30 profit margin 99% (TrustMRR snapshot) For sale: asking $200,000 (2.9x), first listed 9 Mar 2026, 10 offers received Monthly range Nov 2025 → Sep 2026: $4,586 – $6,402 (no cliff; Oct MTD $3,218) Revenue synced 18 October 2026 ~05:47 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Same weekly-pass model for another gatekeeping exam: Polish B1 citizenship exam, Goethe/TestDaF German, or Cambridge B2/C1 — one checker, priced weekly for the cram period.
companies.whyItPrints: Exam prep is evergreen: every year a new cohort of students needs the same score to emigrate or study abroad. One narrow job (grade an IELTS essay), SEO-driven, and a near-zero cost base. Monthly revenue has sat at ~$5–6k for a full year.

companies.name: Bali Villa Hub
companies.description: Directory comparing 3,000+ Bali villa rentals from 100+ verified agencies, agents and owners — monthly and yearly long-term rentals with direct contact and $0 booking fees (company-stated). Homepage also shows "List Property", "Relocation packages" and "Services" (seen on homepage). Founded Jun 2025, registered in Ireland. 86 active subscriptions — the revenue model isn't spelled out publicly; the subscription count suggests paid listings by agencies/owners (my inference, not stated).
companies.evidence: MRR $5,139 · 86 active subscriptions Last 30 days $7,441 (+27.1%) · last 3 months $18,716 · last 6 months $30,775 Last 12 months $49,622 · all-time $50,431 Monthly: $2,088 (Nov 2025) → $3,248 (Mar) → $4,979 (Jul) → $6,473 (Sep 2026); Oct MTD $4,648. No cliff. Revenue synced 18 October 2026 ~04:05 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Copy the pattern for a city where long-term rentals still live in Facebook groups (expat Warsaw/Kraków, Lisbon, Tbilisi, Da Nang). Free to browse, agencies pay monthly to list.
companies.whyItPrints: "Tired of searching through Facebook groups?" — a directory that replaces a messy Facebook-group market. Classic boring marketplace-lite: listings in, leads out, recurring fees from the supply side. Twelve months of steady growth.

companies.name: Getlead
companies.description: B2B lead-generation platform: access to 420M+ global contacts, lead scraping via your own API, and outreach "with up to 99% inbox delivery" in one tool (company-stated). Pricing: Starter €19.90/mo, Freelancer & Founder €99.90/mo, Agency+ €199.90/mo (company-stated). Claims 12,400+ teams (founder-stated). Founded Oct 2025, Poland. 51 active subscriptions; L30 profit margin 60%.
companies.evidence: MRR $2,098 · 51 active subscriptions Last 30 days $11,334 (+25.0%) · last 3 months $28,025 · last 6 months $56,301 Last 12 months $98,079 · all-time $100,279 L30 profit margin 60% (TrustMRR snapshot) Note: lumpy months — $11,431 (Dec 2025), $2,645 (Feb), ~$11k (Apr–May), $5,651 (Aug), $10,754 (Sep), $8,244 Oct MTD. MRR snapshot is far below L30, so most cash is non-recurring. Revenue synced 18 October 2026 ~05:30 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Narrow it: one verified B2B database for one country or vertical (Polish companies from KRS/CEIDG + verified emails, or EU dental clinics), sold as credit packs. Data sourcing and GDPR are the moat and the risk.
companies.whyItPrints: Lists of emails plus a sending tool — the oldest B2B purchase on the internet. Revenue is lumpy (likely annual plans/credit packs: L30 far above the MRR snapshot), but it crossed $100k all-time in under a year from Poland.

companies.name: Sonar
companies.description: ASO dashboard for iOS App Store and Google Play: keyword research (popularity and difficulty), daily rank tracking, competitor and keyword-gap analysis, review monitoring, app revenue estimates (company-stated). From $25/mo for up to 10 apps, both stores, full history (company-stated). ~202 estimated users (founder-stated). Founded Mar 2026, Slovakia. 184 active subscriptions.
companies.evidence: MRR $3,976 · 184 active subscriptions Last 30 days $4,565 (+25.6%) · last 3 months $11,169 · last 6 months $14,604 Last 12 months $14,689 · all-time $14,689 Monthly: $115 (Apr 2026) → $1,389 (Jun) → $3,048 (Aug) → $4,325 (Sep); Oct MTD $2,314. No cliff. Revenue synced 18 October 2026 ~05:54 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Rank tracker for a different store: Shopify App Store, Chrome Web Store, WordPress.org plugins, or Google Maps local rank for a Polish city. Same daily-check habit, $25/mo.
companies.whyItPrints: Rank tracking is a habit product — devs check it daily and keep paying. Cheap entry price for indies, priced under the AppTweak/Sensor Tower tier. Went from $0 to ~$4k MRR in about six months.

companies.name: HelpStay
companies.description: Work-exchange platform connecting hosts with travellers who help in exchange for food and accommodation — "Give a little help, stay for free", 2500+ volunteer stays in 100+ countries (company-stated). Founded Apr 2014, Ireland. 625 active subscriptions; ~2,500 estimated users (founder-stated).
companies.evidence: MRR $2,594 · 625 active subscriptions Last 30 days $2,726 (+7.2%) · last 3 months $7,632 · last 6 months $18,445 Last 12 months $35,674 · all-time $439,748 Note: all-time far above current run-rate — ~$440k AT vs ~$36k last 12 months, so the bigger years are behind it. Monthly range Nov 2025 → Sep 2026: $2,013 – $4,680 (Oct MTD $1,233). Revenue synced 18 October 2026 ~04:40 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Membership directories in two-sided "barter" niches still print slowly: house-sitting in Poland/CEE, farm stays for students, au-pair matching. Charge the side with more demand.
companies.whyItPrints: A 12-year-old membership directory in the Workaway/WWOOF lane. Listings are user-generated, travellers pay to contact hosts. Not growing, but still paying ~$2–4k every month after a decade.

companies.name: Elyx AI
companies.description: B2B Excel add-in with an AI agent that runs finance workflows (consolidation, reporting, variance analysis) directly in Excel, "every formula verifiable, every cell traceable" (company-stated). Targets accounting firms, industrial SMEs, freelance controllers, SME CFOs and chartered accountants in France. Pricing: Starter €29/mo, Pro €59/mo, Team €119/mo (company-stated). Founded Jun 2023, France. 128 active subscriptions; L30 profit margin 65%. It has "AI" in the name, but the buyer and the job are pure accounting glue.
companies.evidence: MRR $2,744 · 128 active subscriptions Last 30 days $6,513 (+667.1%) · last 3 months $9,429 · last 6 months $19,359 Last 12 months $53,020 · all-time $74,011 For sale: asking $79,000 (1.0x), first listed 27 May 2026, 8 offers received Note: spike-then-cliff, now bouncing — $18,819 (Feb 2026) → $7,306 (Apr) → ~$1.1k (Aug–Sep) → $5,910 Oct MTD. Revenue synced 18 October 2026 ~00:41 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Excel/Google Sheets add-in for one local accounting chore: Polish JPK/KSeF reconciliation, VAT split-payment checks, or bank-statement matching. Per-seat, sold to biura rachunkowe (accounting offices).
companies.whyItPrints: Finance teams live in Excel and won't leave. An add-in that sits inside the spreadsheet (not another web app) is the Conductor pattern: meet the legacy tool where it already is. Seller says the recent dip is because he stepped back to do consulting, "not a product issue" (seller-stated).

companies.name: SportsApi Pro
companies.description: Unified API for real-time scores, match events, lineups, standings, historical data and odds across 20–25+ sports and 15,000–25,000+ competitions (company-stated; the profile lists both figures). Target: developers building live sports products. Founded Dec 2025. 100 active subscriptions; L30 profit margin 80%.
companies.evidence: MRR $4,556 · 100 active subscriptions Last 30 days $4,964 (-8.8%) · last 3 months $13,233 · last 6 months $19,599 Last 12 months $21,745 · all-time $21,745 L30 profit margin 80% (TrustMRR snapshot) For sale: asking $59,000 (1.0x), first listed 12 Feb 2026, 24 offers received Monthly: $534 (Feb 2026) → $1,475 (May) → $3,085 (Aug) → $5,893 (Sep); Oct MTD $3,530. Revenue synced 18 October 2026 ~05:23 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Data-API reseller for a boring dataset nobody packages well: Polish public tenders, EU fuel prices, KRS company changes. Note: check the upstream data licence before buying or copying.
companies.whyItPrints: Data resale with a clean API on top. Developers pay monthly and rarely rip out a working data feed. Grew from $60 to ~$5.9k/month in nine months; seller wants out to focus elsewhere (seller-stated).

companies.name: TRADElube
companies.description: Integration platform + PIM that connects three ERP systems with Shopware, WooCommerce and Shopify and handles the whole product-data flow from backend to shop (founder-stated). Core niche: e-bike/bike retail (battery size, frame size, gearing etc.), expanding to electronics and tool retail. Solo founder Florian Feilmeier, Upper Austria, running it next to a 12-hour/week developer job; "in production since 2020" (homepage). Pricing: €79/mo (ERP → Shopware), €99/mo (WooCommerce), €149/mo (Shopify) (founder-stated). Built on .NET/Blazor + MariaDB Galera on Kubernetes (founder-stated).
companies.evidence: €4,700 MRR from ~60 customers (founder-stated) No meaningful marketing in five years; first push is 20 handwritten letters/week to tool retailers (founder-stated) Note: not Stripe-verified.
companies.indieAngle: Pick one ERP popular with Polish SMB retailers (Subiekt GT / Comarch Optima / enova) and sell a traced, flat-price sync to WooCommerce/Shopify/Allegro. Ask the ERP resellers for referrals — they want their product to look better.
companies.whyItPrints: Peak Conductor energy — glue between an old ERP and a web shop. Growth for five years came only from ERP vendors referring their own customers (no commission, no marketing). Support is 1–2 hours/week thanks to per-product end-to-end tracing (founder-stated).
